title: Champions Rise and Make History at the 48th Bank of America Chicago Marathon (official press release, 11 October 2026)
claims: The 48th Bank of America Chicago Marathon took place on Sunday 11 October 2026 with more than 54,000 participants through 29 Chicago neighbourhoods.
Amos Kipruto won the men's race in 2:01:09, with Tadese Bikila second in 2:02:56 and Milkesa Mengesha third in 2:03:46.
Hawi Feysa defended her title in 2:13:33, with Sharon Lokedi second in 2:14:07 and Brigid Kosgei third in 2:14:55.
Emma Grace Hurley ran 2:20:47 for the fastest-ever marathon debut by a US woman, and Clayton Young ran 2:05:23 as the leading US man.
Catherine DeBrunner won the women's wheelchair race in a world record 1:33:16.
The release gives Marcel Hug's men's wheelchair course record as 1:21:34 in its summary and 1:21:24 in its body text.
The men's course record is given as 2:00:35, set by the late Kelvin Kiptum.
The 2027 race is scheduled for Sunday 10 October 2027 and will host the 2027 USATF Marathon Championships.
